limitations: Single source/account/region, one restore per configuration, no indexes.

findings.sequenceScope: All sequence references in boundaryExperiment index boundaryExperiment.calls, not root calls or priorAttempt.calls.
observations: With source 20/2 and write capacity fixed at 2, LastIncreaseDateTime is absent at target read capacity 3 and present at 4, 5, default 20, and 21.

This distinguishes the observed read boundary at 3 to 4 from a rule requiring target read capacity to exceed source read capacity: targets 4 and 5 are below source 20 yet expose increase history, as does unchanged default 20.
All five actual ACTIVE descriptions have NumberOfDecreasesToday=1 and LastDecreaseDateTime; where present LastIncreaseDateTime equals LastDecreaseDateTime.
Initial restore responses are all CREATING, count zero, no increase/decrease timestamps, and expected capacities.

Together with the initial asymmetric matrix, the observations are consistent with a read-capacity boundary above 3 in these empty provisioned tables. They do not prove a universal AWS bootstrap algorithm, write-capacity boundary, or index behavior.
